stemBlocks.value: Triangle ABC has vertices A(-2, 1), B(4, 1) and C(1, 5). (a) Calculate the lengths AB, AC and BC. (b) Hence state the type of triangle ABC, giving a reason.
Think first: Every length here is a distance between two known points, so one formula does all three parts.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p127-q05 from workbook page 127.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find AB from A(-2, 1) to B(4, 1).
Find AC from A(-2, 1) to C(1, 5).
Find BC from B(4, 1) to C(1, 5).

contentBlocks.value: AC = BC = 5, AB = 6, so exactly two sides are equal

strategyBlocks.value: Apply the distance formula d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²) to each pair of vertices, then compare the three lengths.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) AB = 6 units, AC = 5 units, BC = 5 units  (b) Isosceles, because AC = BC = 5 units while AB = 6 units, so exactly two sides are equal.

whyThisWorks.value: The distance formula is Pythagoras' theorem written in coordinates: the horizontal gap and the vertical gap between two points are the two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle, and the join of the points is the hypotenuse. Because squaring removes signs, the order of the points never matters. Classifying the triangle then needs nothing more than a comparison of the three numbers you produced.

commonErrors.misconception: Subtracting the coordinates the wrong way and then losing the square, e.g. writing 4 − (-2) = 2.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Subtracting the coordinates the wrong way and then losing the square, e.g. writing 4 − (-2) = 2.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding the differences instead of squaring them: (3 + 4) = 7 instead of √(9 + 16) = 5.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding the differences instead of squaring them: (3 + 4) = 7 instead of √(9 + 16) = 5.

commonErrors.misconception: Calling the triangle equilateral because two sides matched, without checking the third.

examTip.value: Note that AB is horizontal (both y-coordinates are 1), so its length is just the difference in x-values — spotting horizontal and vertical sides saves time under exam pressure.
